A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LoRDO. Their complete main texts and appendices, including algorithms, equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments at 16M, 125M and 720M scales, downstream evaluations and optimizer ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original batch-size, optimizer, communication-budget and timing comparisons.

M1.justification: The default algorithms and low-rank, QHM and error-feedback updates are unchanged. However, v2 Appendix D.4 adds an experimental Nesterov outer-optimizer variant with server-momentum rotation, whereas v1 deferred investigation of alternative outer optimizers.

E1.justification: SmolLM2 training and the five downstream tasks are retained. Appendix D.7 adds a modeled 10 Gbps communication environment alongside the experimental 100 Gbps setting, extending environmental coverage without adding datasets or language tasks.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix D.5 and Figure 12 introduce direct comparisons against tuned DiLoCo and DiLoCo with optimizer-state synchronization at both 16M and 125M scales. These substantively extend v1's evaluated DDP and full-rank adaptive-optimizer comparisons; DiLoCo previously appeared only in discussion.

E3.justification: v2 adds an equal-token batch-size comparison, outer-optimizer parameter sweeps, and communication-matched controls using either uniform synchronization or fixed parameter synchronization with adjusted state intervals. It also introduces timing evaluation. Figure 2a's stated model size changes from 125M to 16M, without evidence that this retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test optimizer-state synchronization, server-momentum rotation, inner/outer momentum interactions, doubled batch sizes and matched communication budgets. The existing projection-signal analysis is expanded from a synchronization sweep to a joint worker-count and synchronization study in v2 Figure 15.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence-interval procedures or significance tests. The retained figures preserve their reporting practice; the added comparisons do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The original 720M Table 1 is unchanged, including perplexities 10.34 for low-rank DDP and 10.41 for LoRDO-Global. Substantial new results include DiLoCo perplexities of 34.38 and 33.65 without and with state synchronization at 16M, plus measured 100 Gbps training times of 24.23 hours for LoRDO-Global versus 28.96 for low-rank DDP.

T1.justification: v2 adds mathematical arguments for CompleteP transfer under fixed width-to-rank ratios and worker averaging in Appendix F.1. It qualifies earlier full-rank aggregation reasoning, revises Table 3's memory accounting, and derives a memory advantage over Muon when r < p/3 for square matrices. No convergence proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: diagnosing projection failures, restoring subspace exploration with full-rank QHM, and approaching low-rank DDP performance with reduced communication. The added experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations of synchronization, outer-momentum interactions and computation-versus-memory tradeoffs. Its limitations explicitly acknowledge the missing convergence proof and untested longer training and larger scales. It removes v1's gradient-accumulation incompatibility statement and replaces the absence-of-empirical-efficiency discussion with timing analysis.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies fixed rank-ratio hyperparameter transfer and projected-gradient disposal, summarizes selected learning rates and QHM settings in Table 5, and supplies bandwidth and training-time information. These extend documentation of the existing framework; the architecture table, hardware allocation and core pseudocode remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yang (2021) and Yang et al. (2021) to support its scaling discussion and expands comparisons with DiLoCo and Muon. Most research positioning is retained; the MuLoCo and matrix-perturbation bibliography updates refer to works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact. v2 moves limitations from Appendix A into Section 7, selectively expands explanations, revises appendix headings and cross-references, and updates affiliation, proceedings and bibliographic text.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 5 and 9–14 and Table 5. It replaces v1 Figure 8's training curves with the expanded heatmap presentation in Figure 15, substantially restructures the memory table, and redistributes figures around the expanded discussion.

improvement.justification: v1 relied heavily on analytical efficiency arguments and comparisons at fixed synchronization intervals. v2 adds tuned DiLoCo comparisons, equal-communication controls and measured timing, substantially strengthening practical validation. Clearer documentation and explicit limitations also help. The 10 Gbps timings remain modeled, and broad superiority wording in D.5–D.6 exceeds some rank-dependent results, but these qualifications do not outweigh the substantial gain in evidence.
